arch_decisions.title: Student profile fields live on app.system_users (sidecar rejected)
arch_decisions.summary: Add nullable columns student_number, student_id_ext, sec_lec, sec_lab, first_name, last_name directly on app.system_users; do not create a student_profiles sidecar table.
arch_decisions.rationale: Every relevant lookup the system already does (auth, list-students, assign-to-exam, submissions join) goes through system_users.id. A sidecar would force every list/select to LEFT JOIN, and there is no second user-type that needs different profile shapes. Nullable columns keep ADMIN/LECTURER rows valid without backfill. The two external identifiers (student_number — institution enrollment number, student_id_ext — separate external id) are stored as distinct columns with their own UNIQUE constraints. Renaming the external one to student_id_ext avoids confusion with system_users.id which is referenced everywhere as student_id.
arch_decisions.decision: Append the following idempotent DDL inside InitializeSystemTables.extraMigrations: ALTER TABLE app.system_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS student_number TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS student_id_ext TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS sec_lec TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS sec_lab TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS first_name TEXT; ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_name TEXT. Add CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_system_users_student_number ON app.system_users(student_number) WHERE student_number IS NOT NULL; same partial UNIQUE for student_id_ext. Extend models.User with matching pointer-string fields so existing non-student rows serialize as null.
acceptance_criteria: Migrations run twice in a row without error (idempotent).
Existing admin/lecturer rows survive the migration with NULL profile columns.
Two students cannot share the same non-null student_number, and likewise for student_id_ext.
GET /api/v1/users/students returns the new fields when populated.

arch_decisions.title: Default credentials policy: username = student_number, password = student_number
arch_decisions.summary: Imported students are created with username = student_number (institution enrollment number) and an initial bcrypt-hashed password equal to the same string. They can change it via the existing /users/password endpoint.
arch_decisions.rationale: Student_number is required and unique in the upload contract, is what students physically remember, and is already enforced unique by ARCH-001. Using it as both username and seed password makes the lecturer's roster ready-to-distribute. The system already has ChangePasswordRequest and ChangePassword wired, so the post-login flow is unchanged. Rejected alternatives: (a) random temporary password — requires an out-of-band channel the system doesn't have; (b) student_id_ext as username — it is a secondary identifier in the spec and not all institutions print it on student cards.
arch_decisions.decision: Import service constructs models.User{Username: row.StudentNumber, Password: bcrypt(row.StudentNumber), Role: RoleStudent, CreatedBy: lecturer.ID, FirstName, LastName, StudentNumber, StudentIDExt, SecLec, SecLab}. If row.StudentNumber is blank, the row is rejected with a per-row error. MANUAL.md must document that students should change their password on first login.
acceptance_criteria: After import, a student can log in with credentials (student_number, student_number) and receive a JWT.
After login, the same student can call POST /users/password to change it.
Import rejects rows with empty student_number, surfacing the row index in the errors array.

arch_decisions.title: Roster parser: excelize for XLSX, encoding/csv for CSV, header-driven column mapping
arch_decisions.summary: A new package backend/internal/services/roster_parser parses an uploaded file into []ParsedStudentRow. Format is detected by filename extension (.xlsx vs .csv); content-type is used only as a fallback. Header row is required; column matching is case-insensitive with a fixed alias table.
arch_decisions.rationale: github.com/xuri/excelize/v2 is the de-facto Go XLSX library, pure Go, no cgo. encoding/csv is stdlib. Detecting by extension is deterministic and avoids fighting browser content-type quirks (Excel files routinely arrive as application/octet-stream). Header-driven mapping insulates the parser from column reordering by the lecturer. Alias table accepts: 'Student number'|'student_number'|'studentnumber'|'Student No', 'SECLEC'|'sec_lec'|'lecture_section', 'SECLAB'|'sec_lab'|'lab_section', 'Student_id'|'student id'|'student_id_ext'|'external_id', 'First Name'|'first_name'|'firstname'|'given name', 'Last Name'|'last_name'|'lastname'|'surname'|'family name'. Unknown headers are ignored, missing required headers fail the whole import with a clear top-level error (NOT a per-row error).
arch_decisions.decision: Add module github.com/xuri/excelize/v2 to go.mod. New file roster_parser.go exports ParseRoster(filename string, r io.Reader) ([]ParsedStudentRow, error). Returns (nil, err) when required headers are missing. Each row's row_number in the returned slice is 1-based and refers to the spreadsheet row (header is row 1, first data row is 2) so per-row errors are addressable in the UI. Whitespace is trimmed; rows where all six columns are empty are silently skipped (trailing-blank-rows resilience).
acceptance_criteria: ParseRoster on a .csv with the six required headers in any order yields N rows in source order with correct field mapping.
ParseRoster on a .xlsx produced by Excel/LibreOffice with the same headers yields identical results.
Missing a required header column returns (nil, error containing the missing header name).
Empty trailing rows are skipped, not returned as blank-error rows.
Header matching is case-insensitive and tolerant of underscore/space variants per the alias table.

arch_decisions.title: Import endpoint: POST /api/v1/lecturer/students/import (multipart, per-row outcome)
arch_decisions.summary: New lecturer endpoint accepts multipart/form-data with a 'file' part and returns an import report. Upsert by student_number: insert if absent, UPDATE name/section/student_id_ext if a student with that student_number already exists.
arch_decisions.rationale: Idempotency by student_number lets lecturers re-upload a corrected roster without manual cleanup. Per-row outcome reporting lets the lecturer fix only the offending rows. The endpoint sits next to the existing /lecturer/users/bulk plumbing but is distinct: bulk takes structured JSON of {username, password, role}, import takes a file and synthesizes those internally per ARCH-002.
arch_decisions.decision: Route: POST /api/v1/lecturer/students/import (multipart, RoleMiddleware(RoleAdmin, RoleLecturer)). Field name 'file'. Max size enforced via gin r.MaxMultipartMemory (default is fine for rosters under a few MB; document 10MB cap). Handler flow: (1) save uploaded file to memory buffer, (2) call services.ParseRoster, (3) call StudentImportService.Import(ctx, lecturer, rows) which performs per-row work inside a single pgx transaction with savepoints. On savepoint failure the row is rolled back (savepoint released) and its error pushed to the report; the outer transaction commits at the end. Response JSON: {total, created, updated, skipped, errors:[{row, student_number, message}]}. HTTP 200 even with per-row errors; HTTP 400 only when the file itself is unparseable (missing required headers, unsupported format).
acceptance_criteria: POST with a valid CSV containing N new students returns 200 with total=N, created=N, updated=0, skipped=0, errors=[].
Re-POSTing the same file returns 200 with created=0, updated=N (idempotent).
POST with one row whose student_number is blank returns 200 with that row in errors[] and the other rows created.
POST without the file part returns 400.
POST as a STUDENT returns 403 from RoleMiddleware.
Per-row repository UPSERT uses ON CONFLICT (student_number) DO UPDATE.

arch_decisions.title: Repository: UpsertStudentByNumber + extended ListStudents projection
arch_decisions.summary: Add PostgresRepository.UpsertStudentByNumber(ctx, tx, row) which performs the savepointed insert-or-update keyed on student_number, and extend GetAllUsersByRole (or add ListStudentsDetailed) to return the new profile columns so /api/v1/users/students surfaces them.
arch_decisions.rationale: Keeping all SQL in the repository layer matches the existing pattern (controllers never write SQL). Taking pgx.Tx as a parameter lets the import service drive savepoints at row granularity. Extending the existing list rather than adding a parallel endpoint keeps the frontend simple — the lecturer's existing student picker just gains more columns.
arch_decisions.decision: Signature: func (r *PostgresRepository) UpsertStudentByNumber(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, in StudentImportRow, creatorID int) (outcome string, userID int, err error) where outcome ∈ {"created","updated"}. SQL: INSERT INTO app.system_users (username, password_hash, role, created_by, student_number, student_id_ext, sec_lec, sec_lab, first_name, last_name) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (student_number) WHERE student_number IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET student_id_ext=EXCLUDED.student_id_ext, sec_lec=EXCLUDED.sec_lec, sec_lab=EXCLUDED.sec_lab, first_name=EXCLUDED.first_name, last_name=EXCLUDED.last_name RETURNING id, (xmax = 0) AS inserted. (xmax=0 trick distinguishes INSERT from UPDATE.) Update password_hash is INTENTIONALLY OMITTED on the UPDATE path so existing students don't have their chosen passwords reset by a re-import. Modify GetAllUsersByRole's SELECT to also pull the six new columns and the User model JSON serialization to include them with omitempty.
acceptance_criteria: UpsertStudentByNumber called twice for the same student_number returns outcome='created' then outcome='updated'.
Second call does NOT overwrite password_hash (verified by GetUserByID before/after).
GetAllUsersByRole(RoleStudent) returns the six new fields populated for imported students and null for legacy rows.
Calling UpsertStudentByNumber inside a transaction with a savepoint released on failure does not bleed across rows.

arch_decisions.title: Student exam-results endpoints (per-exam summary + per-question detail)
arch_decisions.summary: Add two student-scoped endpoints under /api/v1/quiz: GET /quiz/exams/:id/results returning the student's latest-per-question submissions for one exam, and GET /quiz/results returning a per-exam summary aggregated for the calling student. Results are ALWAYS visible to the owning student regardless of exam activation state (mirrors the immediate is_correct feedback the student already saw at submit time).
arch_decisions.rationale: Practice already has GET /practice/attempts. Quiz/exam side has no student-facing view at all today. Adding it under the existing /quiz group reuses the AuthMiddleware+RoleMiddleware(RoleStudent) chain already wired in cmd/main.go. 'Latest per question' is the metric that matches existing lecturer-side scoring assumptions in app.submissions's idx_submissions_lookup (which is ordered by submitted_at DESC). Always-visible is consistent with the fact that SubmitAnswer returns is_correct synchronously; gating after deactivation would only frustrate students whose exam is still active.
arch_decisions.decision: Routes (added inside the existing quiz group): quiz.GET('/exams/:id/results', QuizController.GetExamResults) and quiz.GET('/results', QuizController.GetMyResultsSummary). GetExamResults: verifies IsStudentEnrolledInExam, then SELECTs from app.submissions joined to app.questions for that exam where student_id = current user; for each question_id keeps the row with MAX(submitted_at) (DISTINCT ON pattern), returns [{question_id, requirement, type, points, sql_text, is_correct, score, submitted_at, validation_details}]. validation_details is passed through as-is — it is already sanitized for student consumption per the existing SubmitAnswer flow. GetMyResultsSummary: returns [{exam_id, exam_title, is_active, question_count, answered_count, correct_count, total_score, max_score}] for every exam the student is enrolled in. New repository methods: GetStudentExamResults(ctx, studentID, examID) and GetStudentResultsSummary(ctx, studentID).
acceptance_criteria: GET /quiz/exams/:id/results as a non-enrolled student returns 403.
GET /quiz/exams/:id/results returns at most one entry per question_id (the latest submission).
If the student has zero submissions for the exam, returns 200 with [].
GET /quiz/results enumerates every exam where the calling student is in app.exam_students, including those with no submissions yet (answered_count=0, total_score=0).
Endpoints work whether the exam is active or archived.

arch_decisions.rationale: Keeping the import inside LecturerView avoids router churn and matches the existing 'all lecturer admin lives on one page' UX. A dedicated /student/results route is justified because the existing StudentView is exam-in-progress oriented (question, editor, preview) and shoehorning results into it would crowd the screen. Reusing ResultTable for the validation_details.actual_rows/expected_rows shape keeps style consistent. No XLSX parsing on the frontend — the file is uploaded as-is to the backend, which is the only place that needs excelize. This removes the need to add an npm dep.

App.vue nav: add a 'Results' router-link visible when user.role==='STUDENT'. Practice attempts: verify the existing list in PracticeView shows is_correct + submitted_at + the practice question requirement, add minimal styling only if missing.
acceptance_criteria: A lecturer can pick a .csv/.xlsx file in the new panel, click Import, and see a per-row outcome table.
Errors array renders one row per failure with the spreadsheet row number and the message.
A student logged in can navigate to /student/results, see a card per enrolled exam with correct/total counts, click in, and see a list of their latest answers per question.
PracticeView still shows the existing Attempt History list (no regression).
No new npm dependency is required (frontend does not parse XLSX).

arch_decisions.title: Testing strategy: parser unit tests + import service tests (mocked repo) + student-results repo test optional
arch_decisions.summary: Go table-driven tests for roster_parser covering CSV + XLSX happy paths and the major failure modes. Service-level tests for StudentImportService using a mock repository (in-package interface). Repository tests for the new queries are deferred — they require a live postgres and the codebase addressing testcontainers for that layer.
arch_decisions.rationale: Parser is pure logic and the highest-value place to lock down behavior with cheap tests. Service tests prove the per-row savepoint semantics without needing a DB by injecting a fake. Repository SQL is exercised indirectly by the Bruno tests in ARCH-008 — adding testcontainers here would balloon scope. The regression-tester agent [7] will fill in any gaps after implementation.
arch_decisions.decision: Add roster_parser_test.go with: (a) CSV with all six columns in order; (b) CSV with columns shuffled; (c) CSV with header aliases; (d) CSV missing 'Last Name' header — expect error; (e) CSV with one empty row in the middle — expect it skipped, others returned; (f) XLSX byte fixture (built once in TestMain via excelize and saved to a temp file or kept in-memory via excelize NewFile/SaveAs). Add student_import_service_test.go with: (a) all rows new -> all created; (b) duplicate of one existing -> updated, others created; (c) one row blank student_number -> per-row error, others succeed. Define a minimal interface { UpsertStudentByNumber, WithTransaction } in the service package that PostgresRepository already satisfies; the test substitutes a fake. No new test for ListStudents extension — covered by the Bruno smoke test.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./internal/services/... passes locally.
Parser tests cover all six cases above; each is its own subtest via t.Run.
Service test fake's UpsertStudentByNumber records calls and lets each subtest stub outcome/error per call.
No test imports a real *PostgresRepository.
